research_decisions.question: The assigned candidate (schedule-sparsity-aware monitoring decision rule) rests on a premise that D1 refuted. Is the replacement candidate — a reliability-based inspection stopping rule using rho = s2_between/(s2_between+s2_est) as the moderator of marginal inspection value — a Q1-level method, or another measurement? Should the line close with an auditable negative?
research_decisions.decision: NO-GO / CLOSE_CURRENT_RELIABILITY_METHOD_CANDIDATE. Do not run the rho test. Retain the inspection-budget results as a bounded retrospective finding, explicitly NOT as a claim that additional inspections contain no information. Reopen only with a separately specified, loss-specific sequential acquisition model that beats a Bayesian value-of-information comparator in a chronological held-out-condition policy replay.
research_decisions.rationale: Codex returned NO-GO and, independently, identified three defects in my own proposed test that I verified on reading: (1) D6's outcome arm is base+[soh_first,soh_last], which endpoint-preserving thinning leaves exactly invariant, so the correlation would be against a constant — the same error class as D3 v1; (2) my directional prediction was analytically inverted — for B~N(mu,tau^2) observed with noise v, reducing v to a*v gives relative risk reduction rho(1-a)/[rho+a(1-rho)], which increases with rho, so HIGH-reliability conditions benefit more, not less; (3) var(slope)=sigma^2/S_xx, and with fixed endpoints adding the midpoint changes neither S_xx nor the slope, so the v2=2*v4 conversion is unjustified. Codex also flagged unresolved normalization-reference timing in the ISU loader (ref = nanmax(v[:L]) uses the full trajectory) and directly relevant prior art: Kim, Choi & Kim 2022 derive inspection schedules from reducible prediction uncertainty and apply them to NASA battery data; Morato et al. 2022 optimise inspection/maintenance planning from updated uncertainty. Uncertainty-reduction plus an economic purchasing threshold is therefore occupied.

rejected_options: Run D6 and promote a significant moderator correlation into a method (invalid test; observational moderator association would not establish a purchasing policy or novelty)

Declare saturation a property of the prediction problem (a finite descriptor/learner set cannot establish that unused observations carry no information; no practical-equivalence conclusion follows from nearby point estimates)
Treat the shuffled-feature placebo as a complete capacity control (it permutes columns independently, breaking their joint relationships, so it does not isolate every representation effect)
Conclude that inspection optimisation is universally unsalvageable (the current candidate fails; the broader decision problem remains open)
scientific_risks: A two-point secant is unbiased for a constant linear slope only under appropriate error assumptions; it need not estimate the future rate relevant to EOL, and extra observations can reveal curvature, knees or regime change
Endpoint-preserving thinning asks whether infilling an existing window helps, not whether to skip a future inspection; the two interventions differ
U is a reference-schedule DETECTION time, so a policy that inspects less detects EOL later and must not receive credit for that
The 3:1 asymmetric log-EOL penalty is a forecasting surrogate; HGB fits squared error, whose optimum is the mean, not the 0.25 quantile of that asymmetric loss
Eligibility uses eventual t<L, a retrospective survivor population; this does not establish deployment representativeness
ISU has already informed the hypothesis and descriptor choices, so within-ISU variation is not an untouched confirmation set
next_actions: Retire D6 as an invalid experiment design; record the LOW-rho-must-help claim as analytically rejected and empirical inspection-value heterogeneity as UNTESTED (not falsified)
Resolve normalization-reference timing: determine whether max(capacity) occurs before the earliest query for every cell, or rebuild with a reference fixed from pre-deployment information
Report exact age-specific eligibility counts and a direct paired condition-level interval for the saved k=2 vs k=6 predictions, with an explicitly stated practical-equivalence margin
Write the bounded closure statement for line D and record it in the ledger
Only if reopening: specify a loss-specific acquisition model using pre-purchase quantities, with a chronological held-out-condition policy replay against a Bayesian value-of-information comparator
falsification_criteria: The policy requires withheld measurements, future normalization, unavailable target-condition histories, or outcome-dependent eligibility
The upper confidence bound on held-out net benefit is below the prespecified minimum useful benefit
The apparent advantage disappears against the strongest fixed policy or an ordinary value-of-information comparator, or disappears when rho is ablated at matched budget
The gain depends on a policy-dependent detection endpoint rather than a common reference outcome, or fails sensitivity analysis for interval-censored EOL
